title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #9

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. To make a very dark tone with charcoal you should (1 mark)
   A. use water
   B. press very lightly
   C. press harder
   D. use no charcoal

2. A gourd rattle makes sound because (1 mark)
   A. the seeds inside knock against the walls
   B. a bow is rubbed
   C. air is blown through it
   D. strings are plucked

3. Who must do the burning when making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Nobody
   B. The youngest learner
   C. An adult or the teacher
   D. Any learner

4. Which players are allowed to shoot at goal? (1 mark)
   A. WA and WD
   B. GK and GD
   C. GS and GA
   D. Only C

5. A chest pass starts with the ball held at (1 mark)
   A. the ankles
   B. above the head
   C. chest height
   D. behind the back

6. How long may a player hold the ball before passing or shooting? (1 mark)
   A. Three seconds
   B. As long as they like
   C. Ten seconds
   D. One minute

7. What is the main reason for improvising a netball? (1 mark)
   A. Because real balls are always bad
   B. To use available materials when balls are not enough
   C. To avoid playing
   D. To spend more money

8. A player who catches the ball must not (1 mark)
   A. pass it
   B. run with it
   C. pivot on the landing foot
   D. throw it to a teammate

9. What can you do to clean your working area after painting? (1 mark)
   A. Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   B. Leave it messy
   C. Throw paint on the floor
   D. Pour paint in a stream where animals drink

10. A montage is (1 mark)
   A. a painting with only one colour
   B. a drawing in charcoal
   C. a song
   D. a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background

11. Which letter has an ascender? (1 mark)
   A. o
   B. e
   C. a
   D. b

12. In ta-te taa taa (rest), how many beats are there? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Three
   C. Four
   D. Five

13. Why should your composed rhythm be your own idea? (1 mark)
   A. To use more paper
   B. To be different from the teacher only
   C. Original work shows honesty
   D. To finish faster

14. To compose a rhythm means to (1 mark)
   A. create a new pattern
   B. play an instrument only
   C. copy a friend's pattern exactly
   D. erase a pattern

15. Which move skips over a note? (1 mark)
   A. r to m
   B. m to r
   C. d to m
   D. d to r

16. Which melody uses only steps? (1 mark)
   A. d r m r d
   B. d m d m
   C. d d m d
   D. m d m d

17. The sol-fa syllable m is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. moh
   B. mah
   C. me
   D. may

18. Leaning far backwards while sprinting will (1 mark)
   A. make no difference
   B. slow you down like a brake
   C. make you faster
   D. make you jump

19. Which muscles does the crab balance mainly strengthen? (1 mark)
   A. Only the fingers
   B. Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   C. Only the ears
   D. Only the eyes

20. Which quality do rolls and balances build? (1 mark)
   A. Reading speed
   B. Balance and coordination
   C. Loud singing
   D. Colour mixing

21. In music, the sign f means (1 mark)
   A. slow
   B. silent
   C. loud
   D. soft

22. The centre of interest is (1 mark)
   A. the main thing you want people to notice
   B. the edge of the photo
   C. the camera button
   D. the middle of the room

23. A subject in photography is (1 mark)
   A. the battery
   B. the person or thing you photograph
   C. the camera
   D. the screen

24. Which of these makes a photograph too dark? (1 mark)
   A. Too little light
   B. A battery
   C. A clean lens
   D. Too much practice

25. Which part of the finger covers a hole? (1 mark)
   A. The fingertip edge
   B. The soft pad
   C. The knuckle
   D. The nail

26. Covering more finger holes makes the note (1 mark)
   A. lower
   B. higher
   C. silent
   D. louder always

27. Another name for the descant recorder is the (1 mark)
   A. soprano recorder
   B. xylophone
   C. bass recorder
   D. drum

28. How many joints does a descant recorder have? (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. Six
   C. Five
   D. Two

29. Of the notes B, A and G, which is the lowest? (1 mark)
   A. B
   B. A
   C. G
   D. They are equal

30. For a good tone you should blow (1 mark)
   A. gently and steadily
   B. with your cheeks puffed for ever
   C. as hard as you can
   D. only in short puffs

31. When should you swim? (1 mark)
   A. Alone
   B. Only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching
   C. Whenever you like
   D. In the dark

32. If you are in trouble in the water, you should (1 mark)
   A. hide underwater
   B. stay quiet
   C. raise your arm and shout for help
   D. swim into the deep end

33. You begin a glide by (1 mark)
   A. jumping from a height
   B. kicking the wall in anger
   C. pushing gently off the wall
   D. swimming hard

34. In the sit-and-slide entry, you first (1 mark)
   A. sit on the edge with feet in the water
   B. jump
   C. run
   D. dive

35. In a glide, your face is (1 mark)
   A. turned to the side always
   B. in the water with the head between your arms
   C. high above the water
   D. hidden by a hat

36. When playing an animal game, you should play on (1 mark)
   A. broken glass
   B. sharp stones
   C. soft, clear ground
   D. thorn bushes

37. Which is a rule for animal games? (1 mark)
   A. Do not push, trip or pull others
   B. Ignore the whistle
   C. Push others to go faster
   D. Play without looking

38. How are indigenous games mostly learnt? (1 mark)
   A. By watching and joining in
   B. By watching TV only
   C. By buying kits
   D. By reading long books only

39. When presenting your artwork, you should hold it (1 mark)
   A. by the middle with wet hands
   B. by one corner and shake
   C. carefully by the edges
   D. upside down

40. Verse 1 of the anthem asks (1 mark)
   A. for a holiday
   B. for money
   C. God to bless the nation
   D. for a new school

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Describe the game hawk and the chicks. (4 marks)

42. Why does a drum sound higher when its skin is tightened? (3 marks)

43. Why should a composed rhythm be your own idea? (2 marks)

44. State three qualities of good feedback. (3 marks)

45. Why do singers use hand signs? (2 marks)

46. Describe the steps of modelling the letters d, r and m on clay slabs. (5 marks)

47. Give four safety rules for animal games. (4 marks)

48. Describe how to play a mini-netball game safely and fairly from warm-up to the end. (5 marks)

49. Describe the fingering for B, A and G. (3 marks)

50. Describe how to get into a crab balance. (4 marks)

51. Why do we use a streamlined shape when gliding? (2 marks)

52. Why is it good to take different roles in animal games? (3 marks)

53. State four rules for playing the hawk and the chicks game. (4 marks)

54. Give three qualities of a neat montage. (3 marks)

55. Give three ways of caring for a digital camera. (3 marks)

56. Why are funeral songs usually slow and sad? (3 marks)

57. State the recorder notes that match d, r and m. (3 marks)

58. When is an overhead pass better than a chest pass? (2 marks)

59. Name the three primary colours. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — press harder
   Pressing harder leaves more charcoal, so the tone is darker.

2. A — the seeds inside knock against the walls
   When shaken, seeds inside hit the gourd and make a sound.

3. C — An adult or the teacher
   Fire is dangerous, so only an adult does the burning.

4. C — GS and GA
   Only the Goal Shooter and the Goal Attack may score.

5. C — chest height
   A chest pass begins with the ball at chest level.

6. A — Three seconds
   A player must pass or shoot within three seconds.

7. B — To use available materials when balls are not enough
   Improvising lets us practise with materials we already have.

8. B — run with it
   Running with the ball is against the rules.

9. A — Wash brushes and wipe the desk
   Clean-up shows responsibility.

10. D — a picture made by joining many cut pieces on a background
   A montage joins many pictures or pieces to make one whole picture.

11. D — b
   The stem of b goes up above the small letters.

12. C — Four
   Each of ta-te, taa, taa and the rest fills one beat, so there are four beats.

13. C — Original work shows honesty
   Creating your own pattern shows integrity.

14. A — create a new pattern
   Composing is creating something original.

15. C — d to m
   Going from d to m skips r.

16. A — d r m r d
   Each move in d r m r d is to a neighbouring note.

17. C — me
   The syllable m is me.

18. B — slow you down like a brake
   Leaning back acts like a brake.

19. B — Arms, shoulders, tummy and legs
   Holding the body up uses many muscle groups.

20. B — Balance and coordination
   Gymnastics teaches the body to stay steady and move parts together.

21. C — loud
   The letter f stands for loud.

22. A — the main thing you want people to notice
   It draws the eye first.

23. B — the person or thing you photograph
   The subject is what you are photographing.

24. A — Too little light
   Poor light makes dark pictures.

25. B — The soft pad
   Pads seal the hole fully.

26. A — lower
   More holes covered gives a longer air column, so a lower note.

27. A — soprano recorder
   The descant is the soprano recorder.

28. A — Three
   Head joint, middle joint and foot joint.

29. C — G
   More holes covered gives a lower note.

30. A — gently and steadily
   A gentle, steady breath gives a warm tone.

31. B — Only when a teacher or lifeguard is watching
   Supervision keeps swimmers safe.

32. C — raise your arm and shout for help
   Signal for help.

33. C — pushing gently off the wall
   A gentle push is enough.

34. A — sit on the edge with feet in the water
   You sit, turn and slide in.

35. B — in the water with the head between your arms
   Keeping the face in helps the body stay level.

36. C — soft, clear ground
   Soft, clear ground prevents injuries.

37. A — Do not push, trip or pull others
   Safety comes first.

38. A — By watching and joining in
   Elders and children play together.

39. C — carefully by the edges
   Careful handling keeps it clean.

40. C — God to bless the nation
   The first verse is a prayer for blessing.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: A hen stands in front and chicks hold on behind in a line. A hawk tries to tag the last chick. The hen spreads her arms and blocks. When the last chick is tagged, roles change.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid part.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A tighter skin vibrates faster. Faster vibration makes a higher sound. Ropes are used to tighten the skin.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for faster vibration, 1 mark for higher sound, 1 mark for the ropes or tightening.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Copying is not fair and honest. Your own idea shows integrity and creativity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kind, honest, specific and helpful. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: To show and remember the height of each note, and to help them sing in tune.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for showing pitch, 1 mark for remembering or singing in tune.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare and knead clay. Roll a slab and cut three rectangles of different sizes. Make coils. Shape a coil into each letter and scratch and wet where they join. Press on gently, smooth, and let dry slowly in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for preparing clay, cutting slabs, making coils, joining, and drying.

47. (4 marks)
   Answer: Play on soft, clear ground; warm up; keep a distance from others; do not push or trip; drink water; follow the whistle. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (5 marks)
   Answer: Warm up with jogging and stretching. Choose fair teams and positions. Check the ground and the ball. Move into space, pass early and play your position. Follow the rules, obey the umpire and thank the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each stage: warm-up, fair teams, checking, playing skills, fair ending.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: B uses the thumb and hole 1; A uses the thumb and holes 1 and 2; G uses the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each note.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sit with knees bent and feet flat. Put hands behind you shoulder-width apart with fingers pointing to the feet. Push through hands and feet to lift the hips so the body is level. Hold for a few counts.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A long, thin shape slips through the water easily, so you glide further.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone gets a fair turn, learns to lead and follow, and the team works better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: Hold but do not pull; the hawk tags gently; no pushing or tripping; stop at the whistle; take turns. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clean cut edges, no glue marks, well-overlapped pieces, firmly stuck and a clear title. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold with two hands; use a strap; clean the lens with a soft dry cloth; keep away from water and dust; charge the battery. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: They comfort the family and remember the person who has died, so the mood is calm and serious.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: If G is doh, then G, A and B match d, r and m. G is d, A is r and B is m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: When a defender stands close so that the ball must go over their arms.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a defender, 1 mark for going over.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: Red, yellow and blue.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for all three, 1 mark for two.
